pages.text: "Mumu, fish!" Quick-handed monkey Taro shouted right into Mumu's ear. They were looking into the stream beneath the tree. Sharp-eared deer Mumu folded both ears backward.
"A whole school is passing! Let's count!" Taro shouted again. With ears folded, Mumu stepped back. A lizard on a branch hurried into hiding.
Excited, Taro shouted louder. "One! Two! Three!" The frightened fish scattered. Mumu went farther away and sat down. No fish remained to count.
"Taro," Mumu said softly, "my ears hear even very small sounds." His eyes widened. "Really?" Mumu nodded.
Taro stepped back and called very softly, "Mumu..." One ear turned toward him. "Yes, I hear you." "You really can! Then Beside an Ear, Whisper!"
Taro sat beside Mumu and whispered, "Will the fish come back?" Mumu kept their mouth closed and only turned an ear toward him; they had heard everything. Both breathed gently.
After a while, fish gathered again, one by one. "One, two, three..." They counted in whispers. Not one left while they counted to ten.
The hidden lizard crept back onto the branch, too. In the quiet, everyone returned. "Whispering lets us see more!" Taro whispered.
Now Taro knew how loud to be: one, whisper beside an ear! Two, tap with a branch from far away! Three, lower my voice if the ears fold! The next day, Taro whispered outside Mumu's porch, too.
Mumu hugged Taro, wrapping his cheeks in both ears. When quiet words could be heard, there was no need to shout. "I'll tell you a secret! Beside an Ear, Whisper!" Taro whispered.
